chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aslam al-Jabalī narrated from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is killed while he has a debt and has no wealth. Do his heirs have the right to pardon his killer while he still has debt? He said: “Indeed, the creditors are the ones who have the claim against the killer. So if his heirs pardon his blood to the killer, they become liable for the debt to the creditors; otherwise, they are not.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: the legal heirs or blood relatives entitled to act in the case
key_terms.الْخُصَمَاءُ: the legal claimants or disputing parties against the killer
key_terms.الْغُرَمَاءِ: the creditors to whom the debt is owed
key_terms.دَمَهُ: his blood, meaning his blood-claim or right of retaliation
key_terms.ضَمِنُوا الدَّيْنَ: they became responsible for paying the debt

ai.seo_question: If a murdered person had unpaid debt and no wealth, can the heirs pardon the killer without becoming responsible for the debt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a murder victim who died owing debt and left no property. It states that the creditors have a claim connected to the killer, and if the heirs pardon the killer, they must assume responsibility for settling the deceased’s debt.
